units.function: Static test asserting the server package build-script string contains shell commands that copy onboarding and built-in Agent assets into dist.
units.dependencyDirection: The test reads package.json directly and treats fragments of the npm build script as the deployment-asset contract.
units.keyDataModels: Package build script and source/dist onboarding-assets and built-ins directory paths.
units.lifecycle: A source build is expected to create two distribution directories and recursively copy both static asset trees.
units.testAssessment: It catches accidental deletion of three exact command fragments but never runs the build, enumerates required files, verifies hashes/modes/symlinks, checks stale destination files or exercises packaged/container artifacts. Exact shell text is brittle and platform-specific.
units.designRationale: Protect runtime-dependent non-TypeScript assets from disappearing during packaging.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS releases must include signed Connector/template/brand assets reproducibly across managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the need for an asset completeness guard, but generate a manifest with hashes/licenses and verify the actual built package/container rather than matching shell text.
units.responsibilityConflict: Copying files proves neither provenance nor that the shipped assets match an approved release digest.
evidence: d166069b Preserve built-in agent assets in server builds (#9339)

units.function: Unit tests for recognizing PostgreSQL unique-constraint violations across postgres.js, node-postgres and Drizzle wrapper shapes.
units.dependencyDirection: Unknown thrown values and an optional expected constraint name flow into a database-neutral route helper that walks cause links and inspects driver codes/fields/messages.
units.keyDataModels: SQLSTATE 23505, constraint/constraint_name, driver message and recursive cause.
units.lifecycle: The helper matches direct or wrapped unique violations, optionally narrows to one constraint, falls back to driver text when structured names are absent and terminates cyclic cause chains.
units.testAssessment: Good compatibility and adversarial coverage includes multiple drivers, wrapping, other constraints/codes, nulls and self-referential causes. Missing are deep-chain bounds, aggregate errors, localized/truncated messages, spoofed plain objects and preservation of the original error/evidence.
units.designRationale: Map expected database races to stable application conflicts despite ORM/driver error-shape variation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deterministic idempotency/conflict outcomes across cloud and local database adapters without leaking vendor errors into application contracts.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT behind DataStorePort with stable conflict codes and structured adapter mapping; use message parsing only as a last-resort telemetry signal, not an authorization or correctness guarantee.
units.responsibilityConflict: A uniqueness conflict identifies a race, not which command or responsible actor won; application events must still record the authoritative winner and rejected intent.
evidence: 6a4e2e1b fix(routes): return 409 for routine checkout conflicts (#3790)

units.function: Unit tests distinguishing a wrapped database ECONNREFUSED from ordinary feedback-export failures without trusting top-level message text.
units.dependencyDirection: Application flush-control logic inspects structured nested error codes to decide whether database unavailability should alter feedback export behavior.
units.keyDataModels: Error/cause chain, ECONNREFUSED code and ordinary upstream failure.
units.lifecycle: A driver connection-refused cause is classified as database unavailable; upload failures and user-controlled text mentioning the same token are not.
units.testAssessment: The negative untrusted-message case is valuable. Coverage is narrow: no nested depth/cycles, timeout/reset/DNS/TLS errors, SQLSTATE shutdown codes, pool errors, retry policy, cancellation or flush durability/loss assertions.
units.designRationale: Avoid misclassifying telemetry/export content as control-plane database failure while shutting down or recovering.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS audit/evidence export must distinguish durable-store outages from sink failures and never lose responsibility records because optional telemetry failed.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT structured adapter error families, but keep audit evidence in a durable outbox with independent retry/dead-letter health; optional feedback must never own core lifecycle control.
units.responsibilityConflict: Classification alone does not prove whether feedback/evidence was persisted, retried or lost, nor who is accountable for a degraded audit sink.

units.function: Unit guard proving Issue subtree control rejects a root outside the requested Company before descendant traversal.
units.dependencyDirection: Company and root Issue IDs enter a service; one root lookup establishes tenant ownership before any recursive pause/cancel/restore traversal.
units.keyDataModels: Company ID, root Issue ID, pause mode and 404 service error.
units.lifecycle: A missing root in the Company scope returns not found after one query and performs no descendant traversal.
units.testAssessment: The fail-closed ordering is valuable but only one empty-select negative path is covered. Missing are positive trees, cycles/depth/size limits, mixed-Company corrupt descendants, concurrent mutation, partial pause/cancel/restore, authorization, transactions and evidence events.
units.designRationale: Prevent cross-tenant graph traversal and information disclosure before performing potentially large recursive control operations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs organization-scoped Work graph controls whose pause/cancel effects are bounded, atomic or recoverable and attributable to an authorized human.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT tenant-root validation before traversal and not-found concealment; add policy authorization, bounded graph snapshots, plan/digest approval, idempotent execution and per-node outcome evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service guard proves tenant scope only; it does not bind a destructive subtree action to an accountable actor, approved target set or recovery plan.
evidence: f98c348e [codex] Add issue subtree pause, cancel, and restore controls (#4332)
